message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"11","text":"Therefore, since you truly are disciples of a prophet, lay aside the discord from which wrongdoing arises and eagerly undertake to do good. But if any of you doubts that what has been said will happen, let him admit it without shame, provided he cares for his own soul, and he will be fully assured by the one who presides. But if he has believed rightly, let him confidently conduct his life as one fleeing a great fire of condemnation and entering God’s everlasting, good kingdom.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"προφήτου ἀληθῶς ὄντες μαθηταί","chosen":"since you truly are disciples of a prophet","rationale":"Takes ἀληθῶς with ὄντες, emphasizing that they truly are disciples, while leaving the prophet unnamed as in the Greek."},{"source_quote":"τὸ εὖ ποιεῖν ἀναδέξασθε","chosen":"eagerly undertake to do good","rationale":"ἀναδέχομαι conveys taking a responsibility upon oneself, not merely beginning an action."},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ τοῦ προεστῶτος πληροφορηθήσεται","chosen":"he will be fully assured by the one who presides","rationale":"πληροφορέω denotes bringing someone to full assurance; προεστώς identifies the presiding leader without specifying another title."},{"source_quote":"πολιτευέσθω","chosen":"let him confidently conduct his life","rationale":"The verb concerns one’s manner of life or conduct, with θαρρῶν supplying confidence."},{"source_quote":"εἰς ἀιδίαν ἀγαθὴν θεοῦ βασιλείαν","chosen":"entering God’s everlasting, good kingdom","rationale":"Preserves both adjectives, ἀιδίαν and ἀγαθήν, rather than allowing one to absorb the other."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"12","text":"The deacons of the church, then, should be the bishop’s eyes, moving about discerningly and examining the actions of each person in the church to see who is about to sin, so that, when caught by the admonition of the one who presides, he perhaps may not go through with the sin at all. They should bring back those who desert their posts, preventing those who gather from failing to listen to the discourses, so that they may be able, by the word of truth, to cleanse away the discouragements that from time to time fall upon the heart from both life’s misfortunes and evil associations. For when they remain uncultivated for a long time, they become material for fire. They should also learn who are ill in the flesh and report them to the unaware multitude so that they may be made known, and they should provide what is needed according to the judgment of the one who presides. Even if they do this without his knowledge, they do not sin. The deacons, then, should take thought for these and similar matters.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"συνετῶς ῥεμβόμενοι","chosen":"moving about discerningly","rationale":"Although ῥέμβομαι can suggest wandering, the adverb and the deacons’ function as the bishop’s eyes indicate purposeful movement and observation."},{"source_quote":"πολυπραγμονοῦντες τὰς πράξεις","chosen":"examining the actions","rationale":"πολυπραγμονέω can imply intrusive scrutiny; here it describes close investigation undertaken to prevent wrongdoing."},{"source_quote":"τάχα οὐ μὴ τελέσῃ τὸ ἁμάρτημα","chosen":"he perhaps may not go through with the sin at all","rationale":"τάχα introduces possibility, while οὐ μή gives emphatic force to the negative and τελέσῃ denotes carrying the act to completion."},{"source_quote":"τοὺς λειποτάκτας","chosen":"those who desert their posts","rationale":"λειποτάκτης is a military image for a deserter, retained here for members abandoning their appointed place."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ μὴ ἐπιλείπειν τοὺς συνερχομένους τῶν λόγων ἐπακούειν","chosen":"preventing those who gather from failing to listen to the discourses","rationale":"Treats τοὺς συνερχομένους as the understood subject of the infinitival construction and ἐπακούειν as complementary to ἐπιλείπειν."},{"source_quote":"χρόνῳ πολλῷ χερσεύσωσιν","chosen":"remain uncultivated for a long time","rationale":"χερσεύω uses the image of land lying untilled or fallow."},{"source_quote":"πυρὸς ἔργον γίνονται","chosen":"they become material for fire","rationale":"The rendering preserves the fire image while expressing the idiomatic sense of something becoming fire’s material or prey."},{"source_quote":"κατὰ σάρκα νοσοῦντας","chosen":"ill in the flesh","rationale":"Retains the explicit σάρξ language distinguishing bodily sickness from another kind of affliction."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τῇ τοῦ προκαθεζομένου γνώμῃ","chosen":"according to the judgment of the one who presides","rationale":"γνώμη here denotes the presiding leader’s considered decision or authorization."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"καὶ τῷ ἀγνοοῦντι πλήθει προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν, ἵν’ ἐπιφαίνωνται","issue":"The rare verb προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν and the unstated subject of ἐπιφαίνωνται leave the precise action and antecedent uncertain. The translation understands the sick people as being reported to the unaware multitude and thereby made known, but the clause could instead envisage the multitude or the deacons making an appearance.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true}]},{"reference":"13","text":"Those who catechize should first be catechized and then catechize others, for the work concerns human souls. The instructor in the discourses must adapt himself to the many dispositions of those who are learning. The one who catechizes must therefore be widely learned, above reproach, highly experienced, and fearless, as you yourselves will find Clement—who is to catechize after me—to be. For it would take too long for me now to discuss the matter item by item. Nevertheless, if you are of one mind, you will be able to be carried into the harbor of rest, where there is the peaceful city of a great king.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"οἱ κατηχοῦντες πρῶτον κατηχήθέντες κατηχείτωσαν","chosen":"Those who catechize should first be catechized and then catechize others","rationale":"Preserves the repeated κατηχέω word family and the requirement that instructors first receive instruction themselves."},{"source_quote":"περὶ ψυχῆς ἀνθρώπων τὸ ἔργον","chosen":"the work concerns human souls","rationale":"Expresses the collective force of the singular ψυχῆς with the plural genitive ἀνθρώπων in natural English."},{"source_quote":"πρὸς γὰρ τὰς πολλὰς τῶν μανθανόντων γνώμας συναρμόζεσθαι","chosen":"must adapt himself to the many dispositions of those who are learning","rationale":"γνώμαι here are the learners’ differing outlooks or dispositions, and συναρμόζεσθαι calls for fitting the instruction to them."},{"source_quote":"πολυμαθῆ οὖν καὶ ἀνεπίληπτον πολύπειρόν τε καὶ ἄδειλον","chosen":"widely learned, above reproach, highly experienced, and fearless","rationale":"Keeps all four qualifications in their source order."},{"source_quote":"ὡς αὐτοὶ εἴσεσθε Κλήμεντα μετ’ ἐμὲ κατηχεῖν μέλλοντα","chosen":"as you yourselves will find Clement—who is to catechize after me—to be","rationale":"The Greek leaves the earlier predicates understood after Κλήμεντα; the English makes that ellipsis intelligible without adding a new qualification."},{"source_quote":"τὸ κατ’ εἶδος λέγειν","chosen":"to discuss the matter item by item","rationale":"κατ’ εἶδος denotes treating the particulars individually or in detail."},{"source_quote":"εἰς τὸν τῆς ἀναπαύσεως ἐνεχθῆναι λιμένα","chosen":"to be carried into the harbor of rest","rationale":"Retains the passive nautical image that leads directly into the extended ship comparison of the following section."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"14","text":"For the whole enterprise of the church resembles a large ship carrying through a fierce storm men who are from many places and who wish to inhabit one particular city belonging to a good kingdom. Let God, then, be the master of this ship for you, and let the helmsman be likened to the Messiah, the bow officer to the bishop, the sailors to the elders, the officers of the ship’s sides to the deacons, the ship’s recruiters to those who catechize, the multitude of the brothers to the passengers, the deep sea to the world, and the contrary winds to the temptations. Let the persecutions, dangers, and afflictions of every kind be likened to the towering waves; the winds blowing out from land in the storms, and the gusts, to the discourses of deceivers and false prophets; the promontories and rough places to judges in positions of authority who threaten terrible things; and places between two seas and beast-infested places to those who are irrational and doubtful about the promises of the truth. Let the hypocrites be understood as likened to pirates. Nevertheless, regard sins alone as a mighty whirlpool, a Tartarean Charybdis, murderous collisions, and deadly breakups. Therefore, so that, sailing with a fair wind, you may be carried more safely into the harbor of the hoped-for city, pray so as to be heard; and prayers are heard through good deeds.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὅλον τὸ πρᾶγμα τῆς ἐκκλησίας","chosen":"the whole enterprise of the church","rationale":"πρᾶγμα encompasses the church’s entire undertaking or state of affairs, not merely an isolated activity."},{"source_quote":"μίαν τινὰ ἀγαθῆς βασιλείας πόλιν","chosen":"one particular city belonging to a good kingdom","rationale":"Preserves μίαν τινά and the genitive ἀγαθῆς βασιλείας without identifying the city or kingdom more specifically than the source does."},{"source_quote":"ὁ μὲν κυβερνήτης χριστῷ","chosen":"the helmsman be likened to the Messiah","rationale":"κυβερνήτης is the person steering the ship; χριστός functions independently as a title and is therefore rendered “the Messiah.”"},{"source_quote":"ὁ πρωρεὺς ἐπισκόπῳ","chosen":"the bow officer to the bishop","rationale":"πρωρεύς denotes the officer or lookout stationed at the prow, distinct from the helmsman."},{"source_quote":"οἱ τοίχαρχοι διακόνοις","chosen":"the officers of the ship’s sides to the deacons","rationale":"τοίχαρχοι were officers associated with the ship’s sides or their rowing divisions; the source’s specialized rank is retained descriptively."},{"source_quote":"οἱ ναυστολόγοι τοῖς κατηχοῦσιν","chosen":"the ship’s recruiters to those who catechize","rationale":"ναυστολόγοι denotes personnel who enroll or muster people for a ship, fitting the catechists’ role of preparing new participants."},{"source_quote":"αἱ ἀντίπνοιαι τοῖς πειρασμοῖς","chosen":"the contrary winds to the temptations","rationale":"ἀντίπνοιαι are winds blowing against a vessel, preserving the nautical force of the comparison."},{"source_quote":"τὰ ἀπόγεια τῶν χειμάρρων καὶ τὰ φυσήματα","chosen":"the winds blowing out from land in the storms, and the gusts","rationale":"The compressed nautical expression is understood as winds originating from land amid storm conditions, together with sudden blasts."},{"source_quote":"διθάλασσοι δὲ καὶ θηριώδεις τόποι","chosen":"places between two seas and beast-infested places","rationale":"Preserves both hazardous geographical images rather than reducing them generally to dangerous waters."},{"source_quote":"ταρταρέαν χάρυβδιν","chosen":"a Tartarean Charybdis","rationale":"Retains both the underworld adjective and the named mythic sea hazard."},{"source_quote":"ἐπηκόως εὔχεσθε","chosen":"pray so as to be heard","rationale":"The adverb describes prayer that gains a hearing, as the following clause explicitly connects heard prayer with good deeds."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"15","text":"The passengers, then, should keep steady, seated firmly in their own places, so that through disorder they do not cause rocking or a list to one side. The ship’s recruiters should call the rewards to mind. The deacons should neglect none of the things entrusted to them. The elders, like sailors, should carefully prepare what each person needs. The bishop, like a bow officer keeping watch, should relay only the helmsman’s words. The Messiah, as Savior and helmsman, should be loved, and he alone should be trusted concerning what he says. All of them should pray to God that they may sail with a fair wind. Those sailing should expect every affliction, since they are sailing past a great and turbulent deep—the world—at one time becoming discouraged, persecuted, scattered, hungry, thirsty, naked, and distressed, and again at another time becoming united, assembled, and at peace. But they should also expect to be seasick, dizzy, and vomiting (that is, confessing their offenses as though they were disease-producing bile—by which I mean the sins arising from bitterness and the evils heaped up from disorderly desires. By confessing these, as though you had vomited them, you are relieved of the illness and receive the saving health that comes from attentive treatment).","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"εὐσταθείτωσαν","chosen":"should keep steady","rationale":"The verb calls for maintaining a stable position aboard the allegorical ship."},{"source_quote":"σεισμὸν ἢ ἑτεροκλινίαν","chosen":"rocking or a list to one side","rationale":"σεισμός is the vessel’s shaking or rocking, while ἑτεροκλινία denotes an unequal inclination toward one side."},{"source_quote":"οἱ ναυστολόγοι τοὺς μισθοὺς ὑπομιμνησκέτωσαν","chosen":"The ship’s recruiters should call the rewards to mind","rationale":"μισθοί can denote wages or rewards; “rewards” preserves the catechetical application while the nautical office remains explicit."},{"source_quote":"καταρτιζέτωσαν ἐπιμελῶς -ὰ χρῄζοντα ἑκάστῳ","chosen":"should carefully prepare what each person needs","rationale":"The translation follows the contextually probable article τὰ for the malformed supplied -ὰ; the proposed correction is disclosed in source_issues."},{"source_quote":"τοὺς λόγους ἀντιβαλλέτω","chosen":"should relay only the helmsman’s words","rationale":"In this setting ἀντιβάλλω describes passing on or communicating another person’s words."},{"source_quote":"ὁ χριστὸς ὡς σωτὴρ κυβερνήτης","chosen":"The Messiah, as Savior and helmsman","rationale":"Both σωτήρ and κυβερνήτης are retained as roles attributed to the independently titular χριστός."},{"source_quote":"γυμνητεύοντες","chosen":"naked","rationale":"The participle means going without clothing and is not broadened into a general reference to poverty."},{"source_quote":"ἐνούμενοι, συναλιζόμενοι, ἡσυχάζοντες","chosen":"becoming united, assembled, and at peace","rationale":"Keeps the three distinct reversals of division, scattering, and distress."},{"source_quote":"ναυτιῶντες, ἰλιγγιῶντες, ἀπερῶντες","chosen":"seasick, dizzy, and vomiting","rationale":"The three participles extend the shipboard image; the parenthetical explanation confirms that ἀπερῶντες refers to vomiting or purging."},{"source_quote":"ὥσπερ νοσοποιοὺς χολάς","chosen":"as though they were disease-producing bile","rationale":"Retains the physiological image in which confessed offenses are compared to harmful bile."},{"source_quote":"τὴν ἐκ τῆς ἐπιμελείας σωτήριον ὑγείαν","chosen":"the saving health that comes from attentive treatment","rationale":"ἐπιμέλεια here is sustained care or treatment that brings the metaphorical illness to a saving resolution."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ὥσπερ ’ναῦται","issue":"The supplied reading places an unexplained apostrophe before ναῦται. No elision is grammatically expected after ὥσπερ, so the mark appears typographical rather than lexical.","proposed_reading":"ὥσπερ ναῦται","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"-ὰ χρῄζοντα","issue":"The supplied -ὰ is not a viable Greek word and leaves χρῄζοντα without its expected neuter plural article. The context strongly suggests a damaged or misprinted τὰ, but that correction is conjectural relative to the supplied reading.","proposed_reading":"τὰ χρῄζοντα","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"ὡς πρωρεὺς ’ἐγρηγορὼς","issue":"The supplied reading places an unexplained apostrophe before ἐγρηγορὼς. The participle is syntactically complete without it, and no elision accounts for the mark.","proposed_reading":"ὡς πρωρεὺς ἐγρηγορὼς","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
